entries.claim: The new Apply-now sequence invokes `risk-check run --staged` without first requiring the just-made fix to be staged.
entries.failure_scenario: A verifier edits a tracked file and follows the stated order literally: make the change, run the displayed command, then commit. Because `--staged` reads the index/tree written by `git write-tree`, not unstaged working-tree changes, the index still equals `HEAD`; the seam refuses with `no-diff` and the workflow tells the verifier to repair and rerun. The actual risk-surface change is never inspected until the verifier independently infers that `git add` must precede the command. State an explicit staging step before the risk check (and retain the command before the commit).

entries.claim: The debug fix path likewise calls the staged-scope seam without directing the user to stage the applied fix before the call.
entries.failure_scenario: After applying an approved debug fix, an agent can run the shown `--base HEAD --staged` command while the fix remains only in the working tree. The seam scans the unchanged index and returns `no-diff`; the new prose treats that refusal as a blocking condition, creating a loop rather than evaluating the fix. The statement that the fix 'is staged' is not an instruction that performs staging; require staging before this invocation.
